title: O Thou Sun of Glorious Splendor
description: O Thou Sun of Glorious Splendor in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 320 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Desiring Christ's Triumph”, where the book credits them to Urwick's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: O thou Sun of glo-rious splen-dor, Shine with heal-ing in thy wing; Chase a-way these shades of dark-ness; Ho-ly light and com-fort bring.

lines: O thou Sun of glorious splendor,
Shine with healing in thy wing;
Chase away these shades of darkness;
Round the world with joy proclaim,
"Death and hell are spoiled and vanquished
Claim the nations for thine own;
Reign, thou Lord of life and glory,
Till each heart becomes thy throne.
Then the earth, o'erspread with glory,
As at first, the Lord's delight.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
